## Fieldwork Update — Golf Course (Gen, Nora, Brianna, Nic, Adam)

- The team has completed 9 holes/sites at the golf course so far; approximately 17 remain, though not all need to be completed
- Site types covered include tee boxes, bunkers, a peatland area, and a crusting site; greens have not yet been sampled
- Notable observations:
    - Densic (little D) features found in the top 1–2 layers; in natural soils, these are interpreted as Superior Lobe till; in HTM on mechanically compacted tee boxes, they are also being called Densic
    - A crusting site near hole 7 shows blue-gray surface cracking/crusting on a dried-out area adjacent to a pond; the surface crust was described as all at the surface with blue and white coloration; Nic noted it looks evaporative, possibly related to upward wicking from subsurface moisture, and is interested to run electrical conductivity on the samples
    - That pond-adjacent area was confirmed as a formerly filled-in wetland (per golf course staff member Brent); cattails are attempting to grow but failing
    - Water table at the crusting site was over 1 meter depth
- Nic plans to come out to the golf course this week; Friday morning is tentatively planned for peat auger coring at the deep peat site using extensions to determine depth; Nic will also arrange another day to sample a green
- Adam will connect with Gen by phone after the meeting to go over completed sites and plan the rest of the week; the goal is approximately 5–6 sites tomorrow using the Giddings probe
- Gen will update the calendar invite with the planned 6 sites for tomorrow and will pick up gutters and field sheets from campus in the morning
- Nora to print 100 RUSI field sheets; Nic to leave them outside the Basic Soils Lab for Gen to pick up

## Bulk Density Sampling Update (Nora, Brianna, Nic, Adam)

- Bulk density has been collected using rings; the compliant cavity method has not yet been needed
- It has been done successfully across a variety of site types including bunkers and greens, though it is time-consuming — typically done when there are 3 or more people at a site
- Brianna raised a question about horizons that are thinner than the ring: Nic advised recording that the sample spans multiple horizons, or using the compliant cavity method for very thin horizons; Adam noted that if two horizons seem similar in density, using the ring across both is acceptable
